full_judgment:
2. Relevant facts leading to issuance of the Rule, in short, are that Habib Vegetable Private Limited, a public limited company, in course of its business, obtained varies types of credit facilities such as project loan, letter of credit loan, etc. from respondents Nos. 2-7. Habib Vegetable Private Limited also obtained a syndicated Lease Finance Facilities from respondents No. 2-7 to establish crude oil refinery project. As a security to the loan Habib Vegetable Private Limited and other mortgaged 532 decimals of lands situated at Noakhali in favour of respondents No. 2-7. Ultimately, Habib Vegetable Private Limited failed to adjust the said liabilities in spite of repeated requests of respondents No. 2-7. In the circumstances, respondents No. 2-7, as plaintiffs, on 19-1-2011 filed Artha Rin Suit No. 09 of 2011 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka (shortly, the Adalat) impleading the petitioner and others as defendants of the suit for realization of the loan amounting to Taka 54,63,82,241 as stood on 31-12-2010 alone with interest till realization thereof. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 5-7-2012. The judgement-debtors having failed to pay the decretal dues, the decree holders put the decree in execution by filing Execution case No.215 of 2012 before the Adalat on 16-9-2012.The petitioner entered his appearance in the execution case on 22-8-2013. On 30-9-2013 he filed an application praying for permission of the Adalat to sell the mortgaged properties by private negotiation. The decree-holders submitted written objection against the said application. Ultimately said application was rejected on 5-3-2014. Against the said order the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 4441 of 2014. The Rule issued in the said writ petition was made absolute on 10-11-2014 with a direction to re-hear of the application of private negotiation. On 26-11-2015 after obtaining the certified copy of the said judgment and order the Adalat fixed next date on 9-3-2016 for hearing the application of private negotiation but the Adalat surprisingly took the matter for hearing on 14-1-2016 and on that day rejected the application of private negotiation. Thereafter, by the Order No.21 dated 28-1-2016 the Adalat allowed an application under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in favour of the respondents No. 2-7 by the Order No. 22 dated 23-2-2015. The petitioner on 15-3-2015, filed an application for recalling those orders, as the same were passed before the due date, but the Adalat by the Order No. 37 dated 7-2-2016 rejected the said application. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with those orders the petitioner moved before this court and obtained the Rule and an ad interim order of stay. 

 4. Mr Mustafizur Rahman Khan along with Mr Sovan Mahmud, the learned Advocates appearing for respondent No.; has been contesting the Rule by filing affidavit in opposition denying the material allegations made in the writ petition contending, interalia, that Habib Vegetable Private Limited is a defaulted borrower of respondents Nos. 2-7. Therefore, respondents Nos. 2-7, as plaintiffs filed Artha Rin Suit No. 09 of 2011 for realization of the loan amounting to Taka 54,63,82,241.00. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 5-7-2012. Respondents No. 2-7 put the decree in execution by filling Execution Case No. 215 of 2012. The petitioner entered his appearance in the execution case on 22-8-2013 and by filing an application dated 30-9-2013 prayed for permission of the Adalat to sell the mortgaged properties in private negotiation. The application was rejected on 5-3-2014. Against the said order the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 4441 of 2014. The Rule issued in the said writ petition was made absolute on 10-11-2014 with a direction to re-hear the application of private negotiation. In pursuance of the said direction, the Adalat, by the order dated 26-11-2015 fixed next date on 14-1-2016 for hearing the application of private negotiation in open court in presence of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, thus the petitioner was aware of the same. Accordingly, the matter was taken up for hearing on 14-1-2016 and on that day the application of private negotiation was rejected on merit as none was present to place the application. Thereafter, Adalat by the Order No.21 dated 28-1-2016 allowed an application under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and disposed of the execution case. Consequently, by the Order No. 22 dated 23-2-2015 the Adalt issued a certificate under section 33 (7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in favour of respondents No. 2-7 rightly, but the petitioner with a malafide intention, only to delay the execution case filed this writ petition and obtained the Rule and an order of stay. 

 5. Mr M. Sayed Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the present petitioners submits that the mortgaged properties situated at Noakhali which are beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the Adalat. Therefore, the initiation and continuation of the execution case in the Adalat situated in Dhaka for selling the mortgaged property situated at Noakhali are illegal. He further submits that if the mortgaged property is sold in auction in Dhaka, there is every likelihood that it will not be sold at appropriate price and for the interest of the judgment debtors as well as the decree holders for recovery of the decretal dues, the mortgaged property ought to be sold in Noakhali as the same is situated at Noakhali. He lastly submits that in Writ Petition No. 4441 of 2014 this Court directed the Adalat to re-hear the application of private sale and on 26.11.2014 the Adalat filed next date on 9-3-2016 for hearing said application of private sale but surprisingly said application was rejected on 14-1-2015 and the Adalat by the order dated 28-1-2016 allowed an application under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and disposed of the execution case and by the order dated 23-2-2015 issued certificate under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in favour of respondents No. 2-7 only to grab the valuable property of the petitioner. Therefore, the impugned orders are liable to be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect. In support of the submissions, he refers to an unreported case passed in Writ Petition No.12655 of 2015 and also refers to the case of Khadiza Begum vs Shahjalal Islami Bank, reported in 67 DLR 583. 

 9. Admittedly, Habib Vegetable Private Limited obtained loan from respondents No. 2-7. Securing the loan the borrower (Habib Vegetable Private Limited) and others mortgaged 532 decimals of lands situated at Noakhali in favour of respondents No.2-7. It is also admitted that the borrower defaulted to repay the loan and respondents No.2-7, as plaintiffs, instituted Artha Rin suit before the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka. The suit was decreed ex-parte and the decree holders put the decree in execution by filing execution case before the trial Court situated in Dhaka. The executing court invited tender for auction sale of the mortgaged properties and since none participated in the auction proceeding issued sale certificate in favou of respondents No. 2-7. 10. The provisions for execution of an order or decree passed in Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has been provided in section 27 of Ain, 2003; section 27 of the Ain, 2003 runs as follows: 

 11. From the aforesaid provisions of law, it is apparent that any order or decree passed by an Artha Rin Adalat will be executed by itself or by the Adalat before whom the order or decree is transmitted by the Adalat who passed the order or decree. To transfer a decree for execution, neither any precondition nor any consequence has been suggested and so, the provision is discretionary, not manatory. 

 12. As per said provision of law, the execution case has been filed lawfully before the Adalat (situated in Dhaka), who decreed the suit. However, since the mortgaged property is situated at Noakhli district, the execution case ought to have been transferred to Artha Rin Adalat, Noakhali for execution of the decree relating to the mortgaged property situated at Noakhali, so that wide circulations to be made by publishing auction notice beating drums, etc., the property can be sold at the maximum price. If the mortgaged property is sold at the maximum price, both, the decree holders and the judgment debtors would be benefited by it. 

 "We have already seen that under section 27(1) of the Ain, 2003 the Adalat is empowered to transfer an execution case to a different district and the mortgaged property having been situated at Naraynagnj, we are of the view that the execution case ought to have been transferred to Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj for execution of the decree relating to the mortgaged property situated at Narayanganj so that the property is sold at the maximum price." 

 19. The learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka is hereby directed to pass necessary order to transfer the Artha Jari Case No. 215 of 2012 to the Artha Rin Adalat, Noakhali through the District Judge for execution of the decree relating to the mortgaged property situated at Noakali.
